page.layout: One printed page of running text, with a running head at the top and a catchword at the foot right. The narrow strip at the right edge is the gutter edge of the neighbouring page, so it is not transcribed.

main_text.p: virtutis studium, & res pro ecclesia, religione & patriâ, seu aris & focis præclarè & fortiter gerendis, sanctâ quadam & libe-rali æmulatione, accederentur. Sic Ambrosius libros de fide Gratiano mittens, ipsum commendat, quòd ab ipsis cunabulis pio semper fuerit affectu, & ad prælium jam profecturus, fidei librū ab ipso petierit, utpote qui norit, fide magis Imperatores, quā virtute militum quærere solere victoriam. Theodo-sii junioris, in historiæ suæ ecclesiasticæ dedicatione, varias virtutes prolixè præ-dicat Sozomenus; ut pietatem, clemen-tiam, liberalitatem erga literatos, prudē-tiam, continentiam, frugalitatem, tole-rantiam, magnificentiam, fortitudinem, temperantiam, justitiam. In quibus en-comiis memorabile cumprimis est, quod de studiis ipsius, & re literariâ in hunc modum commentatur: Fertur etiam, inquit, te interdiu rem militarem, & corpus exercere, & causas subiectorum rite tractare, tum de iisdem exquisitè disceptando, tum quæ æqua sunt decidendo, tum denique, quæ privatim ac publicè agenda, ratione & consilio ponderando. Noctu autem in libros incumbere, atq; in illis perlegendis candelabrum tibi sup-petere fama est, tali artificio constructum, ut oleum

page.notes: The right edge strip shows fragments of marginal notes belonging to the facing page (e.g. "Sozomenus", "Ambrosius"); these are not transcribed here. No page number is printed on this page. The text is one continuous paragraph running from the previous page; the final line "ut" is followed by the catchword "oleum", which is the catchword and not part of the text.
